faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Bronx?
faqs.a: The price turns on the species, the number of entry points, and whether young or cleanup are involved. A single squirrel entry sealed early is a much smaller job than a raccoon family or a bat colony. We inspect, explain the full scope, and quote it in writing before work starts.

faqs.q: Why are there so many squirrels in Bronx attics?
faqs.a: Our crew's Bronx work centers on Norway rats in older apartment blocks, raccoons along the Bronx River and Pelham Bay edges, and pigeons in bridges and roof structures. The pattern follows the housing and the habitat: bronx river keeps animals close, and once one finds a way into a roofline, chimney, or crawlspace here, it usually comes back until every entry is sealed. That is why we pair removal with proofing on every Bronx job rather than just taking the animal out.

Bronx.geographic_features: Bronx River (wooded river corridor through the borough), Pelham Bay Park (the city's largest park, in the northeast), Van Cortlandt Park (forest and lake in the northwest), Harlem River (western waterfront)
Bronx.housing_era: The Bronx is pre-war five- and six-story apartment buildings across the south and center, postwar complexes like Parkchester, and single-family homes and co-ops in Riverdale, Pelham Parkway, and City Island. Old boiler rooms, trash chutes, and flat roofs drive the rat and pigeon work.

Bronx.wildlife_intro:
Bronx keeps our crew busy with Norway rats in older apartment blocks, raccoons along the Bronx River and Pelham Bay edges, and pigeons in bridges and roof structures. Bronx River  gives wildlife food, water, and cover within a short run of almost every roof in town, and the housing does the rest — once an animal finds a soft soffit, an uncapped chimney, or a gap at the roofline, it treats the house as part of its territory.

The year has a rhythm in Bronx. Fall pushes squirrels, raccoons, and rodents indoors ahead of winter; spring brings denning mothers looking for chimneys and attic corners; summer is when bat colonies are most visible in older homes and when young animals start ranging on their own. Most Bronx jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds.
